- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate and should reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.  
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33) in recent days, model tends to underestimate and should adjust upward, especially if price has recently dipped.  
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >85), model often overshoots and should cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or introduce early mean-reversion bias.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 80), model should reduce forecast slope and add downward bias.  
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (±0.33), model should avoid linear extrapolation and introduce slight smoothing or volatility dampening.  
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to lagging sentiment shifts — if sentiment turns sharply, adjust forecast 2–3 days ahead to reflect new sentiment direction.
